item.title: Already Have a Blue Card in Germany or Another EU Country? Moving to Italy
item.description: How Blue Card holders from other member states can work in Italy: short business stays, long-term mobility after twelve months, and what the Italian employer must file.

item.title: Degree, Certificates and Translations: Preparing Your Documents for an Italian Work Visa
item.description: Which documents a work visa and family file need, how legalisation, apostille and certified translation work, and when a CIMEA statement helps.

item.title: Do You Need to Speak Italian to Work in Italy on a Blue Card?
item.description: No language test for the Blue Card, but Italian matters for offices, landlords and daily life. What to expect and how to get started.

item.title: Italy, Germany or the Netherlands? A Blue Card Comparison for Candidates
item.description: Salary thresholds, permanent residence, and employment rules in three EU Blue Card countries, from the point of view of a non-EU professional choosing where to go.

item.title: Non-EU Founders Moving to Italy to Run a Team: Questions and Answers
item.description: You founded a company outside Europe and want to live in Italy while building a team there. How to get a permit, an Italian contract and payroll without opening an entity first.

item.title: Moving a Sponsored Employee from an EOR to Your Own Italian Entity
item.description: When the time comes to open your Italian company, how to transfer Blue Card holders without losing seniority or putting the permit at risk.

item.title: Who Can Sponsor an Italian Work Permit? EOR, Own Entity or Nobody
item.description: A work permit needs an employer in Italy. The options a company abroad has, how long each takes, and when an Employer of Record is the faster route.

item.title: Losing Your Job on an Italian Blue Card: What Happens Next
item.description: Dismissal, resignation or the end of a contract: what you receive, how long you can stay, how to change employer, and what the Blue Card allows you to do.

item.title: Probation in Italy When You Move on a Work Visa
item.description: How the Italian probation period works, what it means for a relocated employee and their sponsor, and how to use it well on both sides.

item.title: Permanent or Fixed-Term Contract: What It Changes for Your Italian Permit
item.description: A permanent contract gives a two-year Blue Card; a fixed-term one gives the contract length plus three months. How contract type affects permit, renewal and planning.

item.title: Why Your Collective Agreement (CCNL) Matters for Your Permit
item.description: The CCNL sets the minimum salary for your level, your hours, leave and notice. For a sponsored employee it is also part of the salary test. What to check.

item.title: Reading an Italian Offer: RAL, Installments and the Blue Card Threshold
item.description: Italian offers state the RAL, the annual gross salary. Why it is the figure that counts for the Blue Card, what is not included in it, and how to compare it with an offer from home.

item.title: Bringing Your Family to Italy: Income, Housing and the Blue Card Advantage
item.description: Who can join you in Italy, how the income test based on the assegno sociale works, what the housing check looks at, and why Blue Card holders can apply sooner.

item.title: Your First Weeks in Italy: Stay Contract, Residence Permit and the Questura
item.description: After landing on a work visa you have a short list of appointments to clear. What each one is, who goes, and what to bring.

item.title: How to Plan a Realistic Start Date for an Italian Work Visa
item.description: The permit sets the start date, not the other way round. A backwards plan for Blue Card and quota cases, with the steps that usually slip.

item.title: Blue Card or Quota Permit? Choosing the Right Italian Work Visa in 2026
item.description: Italy has 43,300 non-seasonal quota places for 2026, but qualified professionals can skip the quota entirely. How to tell which route fits your profile.

item.title: EU Blue Card for Italy, Step by Step: From Job Offer to First Payslip
item.description: The Italian Blue Card in the order things actually happen: eligibility, contract, nulla osta, consulate, stay contract and residence permit, with the sponsor problem solved by an EOR.
